title: Signature Model-Origin Failure Class
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Failure Attribution and Root-Cause Analysis Signature Database (Signature edition), Manon's original counterpart to the public database of the same name. The Signature edition does not copy any public product: it restates the subject in Manon's own Signature framing, as a design that lives inside the Signature ecosystem. Model-Origin Failure Class covers the following in Signature terms: covers failures where the reasoning or answer itself was wrong despite correct inputs and working tools. The record is written as a complete, usable file, with a demo program genuinely executed at build time and its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round.

How the Signature design works

The Signature design works like this: an attribution analysis collects the failed task's inputs, tool results, and outputs into an evidence packet, then walks a decision tree that tests model, data, tool, and coordination origins in turn, recording the evidence that supports or rules out each origin. Applied to this record, the design means the following in practice: covers failures where the reasoning or answer itself was wrong despite correct inputs and working tools. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a Signature reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo counts failures by origin and prints the counts, the total, and the largest origin. The demo program prints:

An attribution verdict is only as strong as its evidence packet. When evidence is missing, the verdict is recorded as uncertain rather than guessed, and the missing evidence is named.
